attributes.name: Company Name
attributes.description: Legal or trade name of the competitor organization.

attributes.name: Company Description
attributes.description: Brief summary of the company's core business, focus, and positioning in the energy storage market.

attributes.name: Year Founded
attributes.description: Year the company was established.

attributes.name: HQ Location
attributes.description: City and state of primary headquarters.

attributes.name: Employee Count
attributes.description: Approximate number of full-time employees.

attributes.name: Revenue Estimate
attributes.description: Estimated annual revenue or AUM/AUA for fund-backed entities (USD).

attributes.name: Funding / Capital Backing
attributes.description: Total equity raised, sponsor backing, or balance sheet capacity. Indicates ability to compete on pipeline volume and hold assets.

attributes.name: Ownership / Sponsor Type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the firm is independent, PE-backed, utility-affiliated, infrastructure fund, or publicly traded — affecting risk appetite and capital access.

attributes.name: Primary Business Model
attributes.description: Core operating model: Develop-and-Sell, IPP/Own-and-Operate, Asset Management, Aggregation/VPP, or hybrid.

attributes.name: NY Market Presence
attributes.description: Depth of existing footprint in New York State: active projects, pipeline volume (MW), or operational assets.

attributes.name: Storage Project Types
attributes.description: Types of storage projects pursued: standalone BESS, solar+storage hybrid, wind+storage, or grid-scale only.

attributes.name: Typical Project Scale (MW)
attributes.description: Characteristic project size range in MW. Distinguishes distributed-scale (<20 MW) from utility-scale (>50 MW) competitors.

attributes.name: Target Geographies
attributes.description: States or ISO regions where the company actively develops or operates storage projects.

attributes.name: IPP / Buyer Relationships
attributes.description: Known relationships or transaction history with IPPs and institutional buyers who acquire completed projects. Directly competes with NEE's sell-side transaction strategy.

attributes.name: NY Incentive Program Access
attributes.description: Demonstrated ability to access NY-specific incentive programs (NYSERDA RETAIL, Con Edison BQDM, NY-SUN, etc.) — a key economic driver for distributed storage.

attributes.name: ITC / Tax Equity Capability
attributes.description: Ability to structure and monetize federal Investment Tax Credit (ITC) through tax equity partnerships — critical for project-level economics.

attributes.name: NYISO Capacity Market Participation
attributes.description: Track record of qualifying storage assets for NYISO UCAP/ICAP revenues, a primary contracted revenue stream in NY.

attributes.name: Ancillary Services / VPP Capability
attributes.description: Ability to dispatch storage assets into NYISO ancillary services markets (regulation, spinning reserve) or operate virtual power plant aggregations to stack revenues.

attributes.name: Revenue Stacking Sophistication
attributes.description: Demonstrated ability to simultaneously capture multiple revenue streams (capacity + incentives + ancillary + arbitrage) to optimize project IRR — core to NY distributed storage economics.

attributes.name: NY Interconnection Experience
attributes.description: Experience navigating NYISO and Con Edison / PSEG LI / National Grid interconnection queues for distributed storage. Includes knowledge of CARIS studies and mitigation strategies.

attributes.name: Site Origination Capability
attributes.description: Ability to identify, control, and progress distributed-scale storage sites in NY — including landowner/host relationships, lease execution, and site control strategy.

attributes.name: Permitting & Entitlement Track Record
attributes.description: Demonstrated speed and success rate in obtaining local zoning, Article 10 / Article 94-c, and environmental permits for storage projects in NY.

attributes.name: NY Development Pipeline (MW)
attributes.description: Estimated size of the company's active development pipeline in New York State in megawatts — proxy for competitive intensity and market claim.

attributes.name: BESS Technology / OEM Flexibility
attributes.description: Whether the developer is technology-agnostic or tied to specific battery OEMs (e.g., Tesla Megapack, Fluence, LG). Agnosticism supports competitive procurement and cost optimization.

attributes.name: NY Project Transaction History
attributes.description: Evidence of completed develop-and-sell or develop-and-finance transactions for storage projects in New York, including known counterparties.

attributes.name: Solar + Storage Integration Experience
attributes.description: Track record developing co-located solar+storage hybrid projects, including shared interconnection and ITC optimization — directly relevant to NEE's hybrid project thesis.

attributes.name: Merchant / Uncontracted Revenue Tolerance
attributes.description: Willingness and financial capacity to absorb merchant price exposure in energy arbitrage — distinguishes well-capitalized IPPs/funds from pure developers who need contracted revenue.

attributes.name: Primary Competitive Moat
attributes.description: Key defensible advantage: proprietary site control, policy relationships, tax equity access, technology platform, OEM pricing, or balance sheet.

attributes.name: Replicability / Scale Threat to NEE
attributes.description: Assessment of how directly and scalably this competitor threatens NEE's ability to originate and transact distributed storage projects in NY.

rationale: The New York distributed BESS development market is moderately concentrated but rapidly attracting entrants due to CLCPA mandates and strong NY incentive stacking. The named competitor list of 17 firms spans meaningfully distinct archetypes — pure storage developers (NineDot, Key Capture), solar-storage hybrids (Borrego, Intersect), aggregators/VPPs (Voltus, CPower), fund-backed developers (DESRI, Greenbacker, CleanCapital), and utility-affiliated players (Osaka Gas USA, Convergent) — each posing a different competitive threat to NEE's develop-and-sell model. A range of 12–17 competitors is appropriate: broad enough to capture cross-archetype dynamics and NY-specific players, tight enough to maintain analytical rigor and avoid dilution with utility-scale-only or non-NY actors. The attribute set is weighted toward NY-specific policy and execution capabilities (NYISO, NYSERDA, interconnection queues), revenue stacking sophistication, and IPP transaction history, which are the true differentiators in this market rather than generic firm size metrics.
